# Results (generated by `python experiments.py`)

All costs are minutes per student per meal (waiting + inconvenience of eating away from your preferred time). Synthetic data; 95% confidence intervals over random seeds.

## E0 Toy games

| policy                                          |   total cost |   ratio to optimum |
|:------------------------------------------------|-------------:|-------------------:|
| Shared live counter (both react to yesterday)   |          3.5 |                1.4 |
| No information (symmetric mixed Nash)           |          3   |                1.2 |
| Private recommendation (correlated equilibrium) |          2.5 |                1   |

Intersection: best CE gives each driver 5.25 vs 4.67 in the best symmetric Nash outcome.

| meal      | day     |   nash_cost |   opt_cost |   minutes_lost |    poa |

| breakfast | normal  |        0.01 |       0    |           0    | nan    |
| breakfast | special |        1.14 |       0.15 |           0.99 |   7.84 |
| dinner    | normal  |        2.14 |       0.33 |           1.81 |   6.74 |
| dinner    | special |        9.71 |       2.14 |           7.57 |   4.57 |
| lunch     | normal  |        1.39 |       0.21 |           1.18 |   6.73 |
| lunch     | special |        4.87 |       1.25 |           3.61 |   3.88 |

Largest epsilon of any reported equilibrium: 14.2 seconds.

On a normal day the four messes lose 132 student-hours to selfish timing (all three meals).

## E6 Correlated recommendations

- Nash-based recommendation: max gain from disobeying 0.0 s (an epsilon-CE).
- Optimum-based recommendation: 13% of students tempted, up to 2.9 min.
- Reward that makes the optimum obedient: 0.35 min per student on average (13% of students get 2.7 min), saving 1.88 min per student.
- Best CE over 26 schedules: 2.235; best coarse CE: 2.235; Nash 2.235; optimum 0.358.
